title: Private download receiver drops DownloadProvider completion broadcasts
reproduction: Plan: signed directRelease on Android 14; delay real DownloadManager completion until after update() returns; watch whether permission settings/installer opens. Not executed.
expected: Download completion is verified once and proceeds to permission or installer UI.
observed: App registers RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED; AOSP DownloadProvider sends from android.media UID; Android 14 rejects cross-UID private delivery. Poller reports completion but does not trigger installation.
fix: Implemented RECEIVER_EXPORTED for privileged DownloadProvider UID; exact action/ID gate; independently query own DownloadManager row ID/status; install only success after existing hash/package/signer checks; ignore nonterminal/duplicate/cancelled hints; cancel replaced receiver/pending continuation.
test_evidence: Ten receiver fixture cases and cancellation regression passed. Opt-in ApkDownloadProviderInstrumentedTest passed on API34: real network DownloadManager success; cross-UID completion delivered once; actual hash verification rejected untrusted bytes; installer handoff zero. Successful APK install UX remains separate release smoke.

title: Cleanup workflow lacks repository context and masks release-list failures
reproduction: Execute actual workflow shell in a temporary non-checkout directory with gh replaced by a function mock; enumeration exits 17 or outputs partial tags and exits 18; assert exact failure status and no delete calls.
expected: Use explicit repository context; enumeration and deletion failures fail the job; successful empty enumeration performs no deletion.
observed: Original workflow had no checkout or explicit repository and hid gh failure inside process substitution; current mock tests demonstrate nonzero propagation and pinned repository on every call.
fix: Add --repo GITHUB_REPOSITORY to list/delete; capture listing in a standalone checked assignment before array parsing; handle successful empty output; preserve manual trigger, permissions, retention behavior, tags and CI protections.

title: A current signed release is rendered as unavailable rather than up to date
reproduction: Plan: install version N; return a valid signed nonexpired same-channel manifest with versionCode N; open update screen. Not executed.
expected: Show up-to-date state while keeping installation disabled; keep lower-version installs rejected.
observed: Manifest throws for equality; downloadManifest returns null; UI renders unavailable. Every constructed Manifest has updateAvailable=true, making markUpToDate unreachable through production parser.
fix: Allow authenticated equal-version metadata with updateAvailable=false; retain lower-version rejection; UpdateModel.update independently rejects unavailable updates before side effects.
test_evidence: Red: current-version JVM case failed before fix. Green: all 31 ManifestTest cases and five API34 model/UI cases passed, including signed HTTPS current metadata, no reinstall, current UI after recreation, and download-state reset.
